pr_title: fix(database): delete indexes before creating if they already exist
pr_body:
### What does it do?

In `SchemaInspector`, make `getIndexes` and `getForeignKeys` required dialect methods.

In `SchemaBuilder`, before creating an index or foreign key, drop any existing one with the same name. This works because extra drops in a `Knex.TableBuilder` do not throw an error _as long as the index existed to begin with_

### Why is it needed?

Should fix https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/22379 and probably any other migration errors that involve indexes, as well as any other cases where an app may have an extra index leftover from some unknown cause that prevents startup.

Note that in a sense it will "cover up" potential migration issues around dropping/creating indexes, but we will be avoiding critical migration errors in exchange for potentially not catching a bug that could cause a one-time rebuilt index during v4->v5 migration, which is not a big deal since that is already considered a possibility during migration. And in general, an unexpected index should not be a cause for Strapi to fail to start up.

### How to test it?

experimental: 0.0.0-experimental.ee7402bacc4656d268ab76aa9c334a7b7a951201

Existing CTB tests should cover most basic cases but

- Test migrations from v4 -> v5 on complex projects and data
- Test complex cases with the CTB creating/removing/updating relations, components, and dzs

## Bug report

### Required System information

<!-- Please ensure you are using the Node LTS version (18, 20, or 22) -->
<!-- Strapi v3 is no longer supported, please update to Strapi v4 -->
<!-- If you are reporting a frontend bug please provide error logs after setting STRAPI_ENFORCE_SOURCEMAPS=true in your .env -->

- Strapi version: 4.25.x to 5.4+, 
- Database: Postgres
- Operating system: Linux
- Is your project Javascript or Typescript: Javascript

<!-- Did you know you can run `yarn strapi report` or `npm run strapi report` to get this information easier? -->

### Describe the bug

When upgrading Strapi from v4 to Strapi 5, users encountered issues with part of the process, presumably when database tables were being modified from v4 schema to Strapi 5 schema and the error below was thrown:

```bash
[2024-12-09 12:55:48] [2024-12-09 12:55:48.957] debug: ⛔️ Server wasn't able to start properly.
[2024-12-09 12:55:48] [2024-12-09 12:55:48.968] error: create index "admin_permissions_role_links_fk" on "public"."admin_permissions_role_links" ("permission_id") - relation "admin_permissions_role_links_fk" already exists
[2024-12-09 12:55:48] error: create index "admin_permissions_role_links_fk" on "public"."admin_permissions_role_links" ("permission_id") - relation "admin_permissions_role_links_fk" already exists
[2024-12-09 12:55:48]     at Parser.parseErrorMessage (/home/app/docroot/node_modules/pg-protocol/dist/parser.js:283:98)
[2024-12-09 12:55:48]     at Parser.handlePacket (/home/app/docroot/node_modules/pg-protocol/dist/parser.js:122:29)
[2024-12-09 12:55:48]     at Parser.parse (/home/app/docroot/node_modules/pg-protocol/dist/parser.js:35:38)
[2024-12-09 12:55:48]     at TLSSocket.<anonymous> (/home/app/docroot/node_modules/pg-protocol/dist/index.js:11:42)
[2024-12-09 12:55:48]     at TLSSocket.emit (node:events:517:28)
[2024-12-09 12:55:48]     at TLSSocket.emit (node:domain:489:12)
[2024-12-09 12:55:48]     at addChunk (node:internal/streams/readable:368:12)
[2024-12-09 12:55:48]     at readableAddChunk (node:internal/streams/readable:341:9)
[2024-12-09 12:55:48]     at Readable.push (node:internal/streams/readable:278:10)
[2024-12-09 12:55:48]     at TLSWrap.onStreamRead (node:internal/stream_base_commons:190:23)
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior (according to what we know currently)

1. Upgrade code base to Strapi 5
2. Connect to a v4 database (with existing data)
3. Attempt to start your app
4. See error

### Expected behavior

Ideally, a successful upgrade


### Additional context

So far, this seems to be happening to users who have existing data in their apps, from what I read: blank applications seem to go through the upgrade process just fine.
